title: Ptosis Masterclass: Clinical Scenarios & Surgical Strategies
summary: A comprehensive guide to ptosis assessment, from involutional aponeurotic defects to complex syndromes like BPES. This poster integrates clinical measurement standards, differential diagnoses, and surgical decision-making based on levator function.

sections.title: Scenario 2: Right Severe Ptosis
content: Right severe ptosis with deep sulcus.

sections.title: Comprehensive Examination Protocol
content: 1. Preparation: Clean hands and obtain patient permission.
2. Basic Metrics: Examine palpebral fissure height, MRD1, MRD2, levator function, and lid crease height.
3. Surface/Adnexa: Look for scars and examine tear film (height and instability).
4. Motility & Pupils: Examine Extraocular Movements (EOM), check for Hirschberg test, anisocoria, and heterochromia.
5. Neurological Signs: Look for Marcus Gunn jaw winking (move jaw side to side) and Cogan twitch (rapid look from downgaze to primary).
6. Fatigue Testing: Ask patient to look up for 30-60 seconds to check for Myasthenia Gravis (MG).
7. Protective Mechanisms: Check for Bell's phenomena, Lagophthalmos, and corneal sensation.
8. Systemic/Posterior: Perform fundoscopy (check for RP, 'salt and pepper' in CEOP) and check refraction.

sections.title: Complications of Ptosis Repair
content: Early Post-op: Hematoma, infection, exposure keratopathy, lagophthalmos, undercorrection, overcorrection, contour defect.
Late Post-op: Recurrence, contralateral eyelid ptosis (Hering's Law).

content.explanation: Lifting the more ptotic lid may cause the contralateral lid to drop due to shared innervation. Always warn patients about potential contralateral ptosis.

sections.title: Scenario 4 & 5 Highlights
sections.content: Scenario 4 describes bilateral ptosis with absent lid creases and frontalis overaction. After surgery, asymmetry in lateral contours may persist. Management for good LF remains levator resection. Scenario 5 involves a 70-year-old woman with gradual obscuration (involutional). Findings: LF 12 mm, MRD1 2 mm, and increased lid crease. Surgical approach for her would be an aponeurotic repair or levator resection given the good levator function.
